title: Optimize automation: fencing protocol, idempotent RPC apply, webhook delivery guarantees & DLQ
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a production-safe commit/fence protocol and delivery semantics for Optimize automation apply operations: provide an idempotent RPC for 'apply recommendation' that can be called from the Console, SDKs, and from automation agents; standardize webhook delivery semantics for asynchronous work and add a durable DLQ for failed deliveries. Goal is to eliminate duplicate/mixed-state config applies, provide clear at-least-once vs exactly-once guarantees for callers, and give operators observability + recovery tools for any partial failures.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New POST /v1/optimize/apply endpoint accepts idempotency_key header and returns deterministic 202/200 with status_url for async ops
2) Backend enforces a fencing token per recommendation batch so concurrent apply requests do not double-apply; any repeated apply with same idempotency_key is a no-op and returns prior result
3) Webhook delivery follows documented semantics: 2xx = ack, transient 5xx/timeout = retry with exponential backoff and jitter up to configurable window, permanent 4xx = DLQ
4) DLQ persists failed webhook payloads with reason, first-fail timestamp, retry_count, and tooling to replay or discard
5) SDKs (Python/JS) expose helpers for idempotency_key generation, status polling, and safe rollback invocation
6) Integration tests covering concurrent applies, duplicate idempotency_key, webhook retries, DLQ population, and manual replay succeed in CI
7) Documentation and API spec published; Console shows per-apply trace and metric (apply_attempts, apply_duration_ms, apply_final_state)
design_decisions: Use idempotency_key as primary client-supplied de-dup token; server persists mapping (idempotency_key -> apply_id, result, created_at) for 30 days
Fence at recommendation_batch_id level: an apply creates a fence record with epoch; only the record with the highest epoch may commit changes; older applies become no-ops
Webhook receipts: accept 2xx only; 429 & 5xx treated as transient; 4xx without Retry-After treated as permanent and routed to DLQ
DLQ stored in our encrypted long-term store (same proto as events store) with a small index for fast query and replay
Prefer server-side reconciliation job (reaper) to detect in-flight operations older than X and mark them FAILED or RETRY based on heuristics
SDKs will not auto-retry applies by default: they will expose convenience wrappers that implement exponential backoff and safe polling
implementation_notes: - Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, Idempotency-Key: <uuid-v4>, Content-Type: application/json
- Response: 202 Accepted { "apply_id": "ap_...", "status_url": "/v1/optimize/apply/ap_.../status" } or 200 OK if idempotency_key repeats previous completed apply
Server-side: create an Apply record (state: PENDING -> IN_PROGRESS -> COMMITTED | ROLLED_BACK | FAILED). Persist idempotency_key mapping to apply_id atomically with a compare-and-set to avoid races

Fencing: writes to recommendation_batch.fence_epoch use conditional update (SQL transaction or lightweight distributed lock) so only the highest epoch can commit; lower epochs abort with FENCE_MISMATCH

Webhook delivery: Use DeliveryQueue service with at-least-once attempts, exponential backoff starting 1s, multiplier 2, max interval 5m, max attempts 10; on permanent failure move to DLQ with metadata
Webhook payload schema: { "apply_id", "recommendation_ids", "result", "timestamp", "server_signature" } - sign with service key for receiver verification
DLQ record fields: apply_id, webhook_target, payload, http_status, error_body, retry_count, first_failed_at, last_attempt_at, tags
Idempotency retention: 30 days; GC job to remove mappings older than retention window; re-applies after GC behave as new applies

SDK changes: add OptimizeClient.apply(recommendation_ids, opts) with optional idempotency_key param; add resume_apply_status(status_url) helper; add sample code for generating idempotency_key using UUIDv4
Rollback: POST /v1/optimize/apply/{apply_id}/rollback authorized only to owner; rollback is idempotent and also accepts Idempotency-Key header
Observability: metrics (apply_total, apply_success, apply_failures, webhook_attempts_total, dlq_count), logs enriched with apply_id and idempotency_key, and traces for end-to-end latency
DB model change: Adds apply_table (apply_id PK, idempotency_key unique, state, fence_epoch, created_by, created_at, result_json) and dlq_table
testing_plan: Unit tests: idempotency mapping, fence epoch conditional updates, DLQ enqueue logic
Integration tests: simulate concurrent apply requests with same/different idempotency_keys and assert single commit, simulate webhook endpoints returning 500/429/401 and assert retry/DLQ behavior
Chaos tests: network partitions between engine and delivery queue, delayed DB writes to validate reconciliation job behavior
End-to-end test in staging: run Optimize flow from Console automation -> POST apply -> verify commit -> webhook delivery -> DLQ replay
Security tests: ensure webhook payload signatures validate; attempt replay attacks and confirm signature + timestamp prevents replay beyond TTL
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy API + delivery queue + DLQ to us-west-2 small fleet; enable for 5% of traffic; monitor apply_latency and dlq_count
Phase 2: SDK release (Python/JS) as minor versions with opt-in examples; ramp to 50% traffic; enable reconciliation job in read-only mode to surface anomalies
Phase 3: Full rollout; enable DLQ replay tooling in Console for SREs and customers; mark old apply endpoints deprecated after 2 weeks
Rollback plan: disable new endpoint routing and revert to previous apply flow; reconcile in-flight applies by marking incomplete applies FAILED and notify owners
